slides.heading: Node Swap
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Node Swap, a very hard linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Swap every pair of adjacent nodes (not values); return the new head.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Swap every pair of adjacent nodes (not values); return the new head.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Swap pairs by rewiring three links at a time, using a dummy head.
slides.narration: Swap pairs by rewiring three links at a time, using a dummy head.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
slides.narration: Swapping values is usually disallowed. Relinking pairs with a dummy head is constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each pair, rewire previous, first and second
slides.narration: Step by step. First, dummy before head. Second, for each pair, rewire previous, first and second. Third, advance by two.

slides.caption: After 0 swaps
slides.narration: After 0 swaps. Next, swap 0 and 1 by relinking.

slides.caption: After 1 swaps
slides.narration: After 1 swaps. Next, swap 2 and 3 by relinking.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: With p at the dummy, while two nodes follow, we relink a and b: a's next to b's next, b's next to a, p's next to b, then move p to a.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: An odd final node stays put.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Generalises to reversing in groups of k.

bullets: Swap pairs by rewiring three links at a time, using a dummy head.
